1: Looks up exact item names, sizes, SKU codes, lots and serials across locations, including zero stock, issued serials, independent measured quantities, reservations and component-kit capacity. Recalled, expired or uncosted goods are never promised as available.
2: Traces every posted receipt, issue, transfer and adjustment with exact before/change/after quantities, independent weights, lot or serial identity, stock cost and the originating native record. Current reservations are shown separately from physical stock.
3: Checks for negative stock, repeated stock reductions and overdue transfers. Growth, Pro and Custom get a daily in-app alert when the check finds issues. Starter can ask for one suggestion.
4: Plans which shelves to count today by warehouse. Uses negative stock, unresolved count differences, recent adjustments, monthly A and B classes, and verified stock value. The daily plan is separate from assignments and physical counts.
5: Reads count sheets and readable shelf tags, preserves the original and prepares exact stock differences for quantities, lots, serials and independent measures. Pro routines require a completed matching example. Custom uses a saved owner scope. Physical adjustments and their value still need individual owner approval.
6: Posts small count differences on its own within the owner-set value limit: counts typed in the app, finished staff phone counts and exact count sheets, lots and weights included. Serials added or removed, phone-count identities or weights that differ, photo readings and anything over the limit go to a person.
7: Sends staff blind count lists in the app for quantities, lots, serials and independent weights. Progress follows completed observations. Growth schedules use an approved example for the same counter and scope. Pro and Custom can schedule directly within the owner’s scope. The owner reviews differences and approves physical posting separately.
8: Shows a blind recount in Needs You when a recorded count difference exceeds your limit. A matching physical recount comes before separate owner approval.
9: Finds dead and slow stock from recorded sales and continuously stocked days, leaving out stock held for orders, targets, transfers and returns. Starter gets one suggestion. Each finding becomes a step: a transfer to a location where it sells, a supplier return request to the supplier who sold it, or a clearance plan whose prices you approve. Growth drafts each step. Pro drafts until you approve one of a kind and save a limit; Custom acts within your limits without teaching. Steps are audited and can be undone while untouched.
10: Flags repeat negative stock corrections for the same product, warehouse and local shift across its bins. Growth, Pro and Custom receive automatic in-app alerts without training and can configure shift start times. Review the original stock movements to determine the cause.
11: Moves stock to the right bin at one warehouse. When staff scan and count a product in one bin while the records show it in another, or two counts show one bin short by exactly what another has extra, the records follow the stock through a bin transfer. A put-away scanned into the wrong bin becomes a move to the planned bin that staff scan. Pro proposes each correction until taught; Custom corrects alone within unit and value limits. Reserved, picked, counted, batch and serial stock waits for a person. Records corrections can be undone.
12: Keeps stock reserved for customers you mark as big, for an expected order on a date, or for a repeating order. Other orders, sales channels and reorder see it as not available; the customer’s own order uses it first, and a one-time reservation ends when that order arrives or on its end date. It never takes stock already promised to other orders, is cut back if stock is lost, and every change is logged and can be undone. Whole-unit products; lots, serials, weights and kits are reserved on their orders. Existing customer orders can also be reserved in full.
13: Shows how many of each kit every warehouse can build now and which part limits it, counting shared parts once and leaving out reserved, held, expired and recalled parts. Part reorders come from kit sales, kit assembly and saved kit targets, including kits inside kits. Growth prepares each part order for your approval; Pro and Custom place them on their own through your purchasing rule and plan limits.
14: Creates production drafts from saved bills of materials and approved limits. Physical component use and finished-goods receipt require individual confirmation.
15: Classifies products monthly from verified stock cost sold. The classes rank real shelves for counts and support location-level safety-stock planning on every plan. Missing sale costs go to review. Automatic safety-stock changes follow the separate job 150 owner rules on Pro and Custom.
16: Plans the yearly stocktake from your rule: the count date, the locations (whole warehouses, areas or single bins) and the count team. On the count date it freezes sales, picks, receipts, transfers and stock value changes at those locations, shares the areas among counters they can reach and sends each a blind count list. A position off by more than your recount limit, in units or value, goes to a second counter for a blind recount. Differences are valued at cost; your sign-off posts them to stock and the books and lifts the freeze. Up to 10,000 whole-unit positions in 50 locations.
17: Starter gets one suggestion grounded in receipt age. Growth, Pro and Custom show recorded lots, serials, receipt cohorts, FIFO layers and proven transfer origins. The owner reviews the complete weighted-average stock position and supplies its supported net recoverable value. Individual approval records the exact write-down expense and lower carrying value while preserving physical quantities and weights.
18: Explains reorder quantities from exact usable stock, commitments, recorded sales speed, dated incoming, lead time and saved targets. Existing drafts, overdue or undated deliveries, missing stock costs and unknown lead-time facts hold a fresh order.
19: Creates native unsent purchase drafts from the reorder list, grouped by saved supplier and currency while preserving every receiving location, exact stocking quantity, pack and independent requested measure. Current source changes stop stale drafts. Sending, buying, receiving and payments retain separate authority.
20: Handles reorders inside approved supplier, product and purchasing limits. Live supplier-mail delivery still needs verification.
21: A daily check works out new reorder points and targets for every stocked product and location, including one setting for all locations, from 90 days of recorded sales, lead time and safety stock. It skips locked settings, new products and locations, too few sales, missing lead times and unclear batch, serial or weight records, and says why. Every applied change is logged and can be undone.
22: Compares saved eligible suppliers by rounded goods totals and recorded delivery time, keeping currencies separate. Chooses the cheapest or fastest supplier through a native reorder preference change. First supplier or changed price/terms require individual review; unclear facts hold selection.
23: Applies recorded minimum orders and adds goods for free shipping when they cost no more than the saved freight charge. Starter suggests. Growth learns from a matching owner-approved purchase. Pro and Custom use current purchase limits without training.
24: Combines unsent drafts for one supplier, currency, receiving location and delivery date when current freight terms show a saving. The replacement retains its product lines and other recorded charges. Growth requires a completed matching example. Pro and Custom can authorize a supplier, location and goods limit without training.
25: Splits native unsent purchase orders by receiving warehouse, saved line delivery date or goods-value limit. Pro needs a completed example for the same supplier, locations and method. Custom can schedule the work within owner-set limits without training. Every replacement stays a draft.
26: Plans purchases against monthly goods budgets by category and currency. It uses dated stock needs, recorded supplier packs and outstanding commitments, and holds uncertain costs or dates for review. Custom can run recurring plans with owner permission. Reviewed plans can become native drafts, with the budget checked again at purchase approval.
27: Orders in whole saved cases, packs or pallets and keeps the supplier's order multiple. Growth needs a matching owner-approved example and trusted item authority. Pro and Custom can use current limits without training.
28: Queues an approved purchase order and its supplier message. Delivery through a live connected mailbox still needs verification.
29: Prepares scoped supplier confirmation requests for reorders and stops queued requests when a reply arrives. Live mailbox delivery remains open.
30: Prepares a delivery chase for a late supplier order and rechecks authority before sending. Live mailbox acceptance remains open.
31: Updates a placed purchase order when the supplier changes the quantity, price or delivery date. The change can come from the supplier's private order link, a reply on the order's email thread, or a saved supplier confirmation, backorder notice or price update. Each change makes a new order version with its history; goods already received keep their price. Changes over your price, quantity or date limits, and unclear evidence, wait for you. Pro drafts until you approve and teach an example; Custom works within your limits without teaching.
32: Finds goods on placed purchase orders that are long past their promised date with no word from the supplier, so incoming stays real. Starter lists them. On Growth, Pro and Custom, under your rule (grace days and a value limit), StockChief closes what is still due on its own: received goods stay and the rest stops counting as incoming in reorders, availability and planning. Orders with a shipment, goods being received, recent supplier contact, a customer preorder or a bill ahead of receipt are kept. Each close is logged and can be reopened; a note to the supplier is drafted for you to send.
33: Refreshes a ready replenishment proposal when stock or reservations change. An approved supplier action creates one purchase order and queues one message.
34: Compares expected and actual supplier arrivals. Replenishment and its purchase drafts use the observed warehouse lead time once enough orders have arrived. Split receipts count as one order.
35: Gives suppliers a private link to confirm an approved purchase, propose a delivery date and send original PDF invoices and ship notices. Buyers can copy the warehouse order link without a mailbox or supplier email. Invoices go to matching on the exact purchase and ship notices stay with its other documents.
38: Plans an import order that fills a 20 ft or 40 ft container by space and by weight. It uses each product’s size and weight or its confirmed carton, the supplier’s packs and minimums, and real reorder needs: products at their reorder point go in first, then the next most-needed top it up, up to your days-of-stock limit. It shows the fill by space and by weight. A missing size, weight or price stops the plan and asks. You can also check a carton layout for up to 20 POs, 500 lines and 2,000 cartons.
40: Purchase orders in another currency keep their own currency. When you place one, StockChief estimates its cost in your accounting currency at the rate of the day. Goods are booked into stock value at the rate of the day they arrive: your own rate for that day first, otherwise the European Central Bank's daily reference rate. A missing rate stops the receipt and asks. Starter sees one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom check rates every day and, when a cost moves past your limit, alert you in the app, in Needs you and by email from a connected mailbox, then clear the alert when the cost comes back. Alerts never change a price or a cost.
41: Turns a short staff request into a decision using the exact saved product name, item code or nickname. The owner chooses a linked supplier and confirms any missing quantity before creating the purchase draft. Staff keep their assigned warehouse access.
42: Tracks reviewed supplier contracts: products, prices, total units and an optional total value, dates and a schedule of up to 52 releases within a year. On each release date the release becomes a real purchase order in whole supplier packs. With a flex range, each release follows real demand from your stock targets within that range. It never goes over the contract’s units or value or past its last date: it trims, skips or asks. It shows what is called off and what is left. A changed price or a changed linked order stops and asks.
43: Fills a physical-receipt review from a supported packing CSV or readable PDF using the actual PO packs, costs and warehouse. A person confirms receipt; no bill or payment is posted.
44: Shows the quantity still due after a partial purchase receipt. Wrong-item and over-delivery reviews still need complete workflow verification.
45: Opens a supplier claim from a checked short delivery, a failed QC inspection or units your team marked damaged when receiving. The email lists the purchase order, receipt, product, quantity and value at the purchase order price, and asks for a credit note, replacement goods or a refund. StockChief follows each sent claim to the supplier’s reply, a credit note or replacement goods, and sends up to two reminders when nobody answers.
46: Staff take photos of damaged boxes on the phone when receiving, on a delivery check or at a failed QC inspection. StockChief keeps each original JPEG or PNG unchanged, up to ten per delivery and 10 MB each, and prepares a smaller email copy. Up to three photos go with a supplier claim as attachments and stay with the claim record. Photos never decide damage or counts.
47: After a receipt, prepares browser-printable product, batch, serial and bin labels (no printer driver) and a put-away list with a bin for each item: a taught bin, a bin already holding the product, or the nearest empty bin to packing. Staff confirm each put-away by scanning or tapping on the phone; the stock moves into that bin through an ordinary bin transfer that keeps its batch, serials, weight and cost. Growth confirms suggested bins until one is taught; Pro and Custom choose bins alone once routine work is on. Unclear bins, reserved stock and changed codes wait for a person.
48: Routes posted, costed receipts and transfer arrivals to confirmed waiting orders by priority, including the remainder of partial shipments. Uses eligible dispatch warehouses, exact batches and serials, recorded stock units and actual weights, and the order’s captured kit components. Physical picking and dispatch need separate confirmation.
49: When a freight, duty, insurance or handling bill is posted for a recorded delivery, splits it over the goods by units, original cost or weight and moves it from expenses into their stock cost. Quantities and supplier balances stay the same. Pro drafts until you approve a bill of the same kind (supplier or carrier and cost type) and save a limit; Custom posts within your limit without an example. Over the limit, unmatched, unclear, foreign-currency and sold-goods bills wait for you. Posts are audited and undone by a reversing entry.
50: Prepares or sends scoped stock-ready updates for previously backordered quantity orders. Live mailbox delivery and separate staff-role routing remain open.
52: Reads a known customer’s order email, PDF or spreadsheet: products by your code, their own code or a barcode, quantities, prices and the delivery address. Growth prepares the order for your approval. Pro and Custom create and confirm it through the normal order checks and stock reservations when everything matches, the address is on file and it is within your limits. A first order, a new address, a different price, an unclear line or an order over your limit waits in Needs you. One order per email, logged, with undo.
53: Repeats a customer’s order from one sentence, in Ask or in their own email, in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese or Dutch (other alphabets are read in English first). “Same as last month” uses last month’s order, “last order” the latest, and “usual” the products in most of their recent orders; StockChief says which it used and prices it today. Growth prepares it for approval until you approve one for that customer or save a rule; Pro and Custom create and confirm it within your limits. A new customer, a new address or anything unclear waits for you.
54: Checks each new, changed or confirmed order through the worker for four problems: stock it cannot fill after other orders, holds and protected stock; overdue invoices or a passed credit limit; a missing or incomplete address, or one that changed since the customer’s last order on business and staff-entered orders; and prices below cost, below the customer’s agreed price or further below list than your discount limit. Problems show on the order and in Needs you with the reason. It never changes or cancels an order.
55: Holds a customer’s open orders when their invoices are overdue past your rule (days overdue, and an optional amount), so nothing on them can be confirmed, picked, packed or shipped. The hold, its reason and who placed it show on the order and in Needs you. It ends on its own when the overdue invoices are paid in full; a partial payment keeps it. A person with accounting access can release a hold or put it back, and every hold and release is audited.
56: Releases ready orders to each warehouse in the best pick order: your priority, the ship-by date, the carrier cut-off, then order age. Ready means the ship-from warehouse is chosen, the order is fully reserved there or in its bins (lots, serials and weighed goods too), the address is complete, there is no overdue-invoice hold and the stock is still there; others wait with the reason. Batch size follows your warehouse rule or its busiest shipping day. Growth proposes until taught; Pro and Custom release alone. Releases move no stock, are audited and undo until picking starts.
57: Groups released orders into pick waves by zone: orders that add the fewest new zones go together. Each zone gets its own pick list in walking order, farthest bin first so pickers end near packing. Lots, serials and weighed goods name the exact reserved batch, serial or weight, or which to scan first, earliest expiry or oldest first. Waves follow your rule for each warehouse: most orders in a wave and the last time to start one. Growth prepares waves for a person to start until taught; Pro and Custom start them alone. Scans, packing and handoff stay with staff; waves undo until picking starts.
58: For each packed parcel StockChief fetches current rates from every connected shipping account and picks the cheapest that arrives by the date promised on the order. Arrival is the carrier's date, or its transit days counted from its ship date or the day it quoted. Other currencies are never compared, and PO boxes only get postal services. Starter sees the suggestion and buys with one tap. Growth suggests until the owner approves one at that price or saves the rule, then chooses alone. Pro and Custom choose alone. A missing promise date or no timely rate stops and asks.
59: Buys the label at the rate StockChief chose through the connected carrier account and the worker, within the owner's limits. Growth buys alone up to $25 a label or the owner's lower $ per label; Pro and Custom buy alone once the owner sets a $ per label; any 24-hour limit applies. Starter prepares each label for one tap. Over a limit, Ask me first, pause, observe or the first 14 days leave it for a tap, and a downgrade stops it before the carrier. Cancelling an order before handoff voids its unused label where the carrier can. Each purchase is logged and never repeated.
60: Emails the customer when a parcel leaves, with the carrier, tracking number and link: once a person records the carrier handoff, or the carrier first scans a label bought here. It goes out once through the connected mailbox. Starter approves each email with one tap. Growth, Pro and Custom send on their own once the owner turns it on; Ask me first, pause, watch-only and the first 14 days wait for a tap. Orders from a connected store are left to the store's own email unless the owner says StockChief tells them.
61: Splits a shipping order that is partly in stock by your rules: which customers or orders accept partial shipments, the least share or value worth sending now and how many parts one order may take. The part set aside goes to picking, kits only whole; the rest waits on the order until stock arrives, then ships. The customer can be emailed. Pro asks until taught; Custom splits alone.
62: Watches every parcel that has left with a carrier, through carrier webhooks and, when a parcel goes quiet, by asking the connected shipping account. It flags parcels late against the promised date, stalled for three days, or reported lost, damaged, returned or held up, once each, on the order and in Needs you, until delivered or marked handled. Growth, Pro and Custom watch on their own; pause stops it, and watch-only and the first 14 days only flag. If the owner turns it on, customers are told about a delay: written for review, or sent on its own.
63: Prepares a claim when the carrier reports a parcel lost or staff report a lost or damaged parcel for themselves or the customer, with the shipment, its value from the order and the evidence. Parcels insured through EasyPost are filed through its claim API; for other carriers you get the claim pack and the carrier's claim steps. Pro drafts until taught; Custom files alone within the owner's limit. Each claim is followed until the carrier pays or denies it.
64: When stock arrives at a warehouse or frees up there, waiting orders get it in saved order priority. Starter sees who is waiting and what ships first. Growth approves each prepared allocation. Pro and Custom set stock aside on their own within the owner's unit limit and send complete orders to picking. Unclear orders wait for a person, and every allocation can be undone until picking starts.
67: Schedules daily, weekly or monthly customer-order drafts from a confirmed source and rechecks prices, address, authority and the chosen maximum for each occurrence.
68: Takes preorders on placed incoming stock within the quantity still coming. Arrived units are held for them in the order they came in; each preorder is then reserved and sent to picking. Less incoming stock flags the preorders affected and you can tell the customer. Growth approves each step; Pro and Custom fill alone.
69: Checks the ship-to address before any label is bought, by a person or StockChief, on every plan, with the connected account's own address check. A label waits for a person when the address is incomplete, differs from the order, is called undeliverable by the carrier, or is a home address for a business customer. UPS, FedEx and DHL are never used for PO boxes. A person uses the suggested address or keeps theirs in one press; a format-only fix is applied on its own unless StockChief may not act alone. Every hold and answer is logged.
72: Answers a customer’s email about stock, a delivery date or where their order is, from your records: only that customer’s orders and shipments, and the stock available now. It never names a delivery date nobody recorded. The answer goes in the customer’s thread from the mailbox you chose for customer messages. Growth asks you to approve until you teach it, by a rule or by sending an answer it wrote; Pro and Custom send alone. A first email to a customer, anything else the email asks, or an unclear order or product waits for you.
73: Writes a quote when a customer emails for one with product codes and quantities: your current prices, their terms and currency, the delivery address on file, valid for the days you choose, and emails it back from your customer mailbox. Pro asks you to approve until you teach it a customer, products and limit on an approved quote; Custom writes and sends alone within any lower limit. A first quote for a customer, a price the customer names, a new address or an unclear line waits for you.
74: Follows up once on each open quote after the number of days you choose, for one quote or every quote emailed through your mailbox, from the same mailbox. It says the quote was emailed, never that it was read. Growth sends alone only for customers, products and amounts you taught with a follow-up you sent; others wait in Needs you. Pro and Custom send alone within any lower limit. Acceptance, a newer revision, expiry, changed prices, contact or mailbox, or a follow-up you stopped means nothing is sent.
75: A buyer accepts an exact quotation revision through its private link. Growth approves one draft order. Pro and Custom can draft it without training under explicit owner authority. The order carries the accepted prices, discounts, taxes, payment terms and delivery.
76: Uses approved customer price tiers, discounts and payment terms for quotes and drafts. The agreed terms carry through fulfillment and invoicing. Measured quantities, recorded currencies and fixed or percentage deposits use their exact pricing basis.
77: Flags comparable cost increases from saved costs, posted receipts and matched supplier bills. Starter and Growth get one price suggestion. Pro and Custom can prepare an exact local catalogue price for individual owner approval.
78: Finds customers with two retained purchases, no open order and no shipment in 90 days. Pro learns from an individually approved private draft. Custom can draft without training under explicit owner authority. StockChief saves one draft and its purchase evidence for each inactive period.
79: Finds companions in orders that actually shipped both products. Starter gets one suggestion. Growth prepares a private quote revision for individual approval. Pro and Custom can add eligible companions without training to new matching quotes within the owner’s customer, warehouse, currency, products, quantities and added-value limit. StockChief uses current stock and native customer pricing, tax and selling units. The original quote stays in history.
80: Checks credit on the draft order before confirmation. Starter shows one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom automatically surface over-limit or incomplete checks and show the draft, unbilled commitments and open invoices against the saved credit limit.
81: Sends a customer their account statement when they ask by email or you ask in Ask: one currency, reconciled to the books, with this month's activity and every open invoice in an attached PDF, only to their email on file. Growth asks you to approve until taught by a rule or a delivered statement you approved; Pro and Custom send alone. A first statement, Ask me first, an unknown sender, another customer named, another period or two currencies wait for you; pause, Watch only and the first 14 days only watch. An unchanged statement is never sent twice.
82: Flags orders with below-cost goods or discounts that differ from the latest saved quote. The owner can review the exact pricing revision, recorded units and posted fulfillment cost.
85: Shows true net margin per order, item, channel and customer: posted sales, returns and credits, minus product cost, fees and shipping. Fees come from your checked import or your fee terms for each channel; shipping from your import or the carrier labels and costs recorded on the order, return parcels included. A missing cost is shown as missing, never as zero, and currencies stay separate. Growth, Pro and Custom keep it current through the worker and flag low margins in Needs you. It never changes a price or posts money.
86: Starter gets one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom build a clearance plan per item for stock nobody needs: up to three markdown steps, never below the recorded stock cost, with the units each step should sell, the cash it should bring back and when, next to recorded sales. You approve every price; it changes through the normal price path and the plan tracks posted sales and revenue against what it expected. Changed stock, cost or price stop it for a fresh plan.
87: Checks every channel's recorded price for each mapped item, from Shopify, Square, WooCommerce and other connected channels, against your catalogue price and your minimum advertised price (MAP) terms. Without a catalogue price it compares the channels with each other. Growth, Pro and Custom check every hour through the worker and flag MAP breaks and price differences in Needs you, clearing them when prices match. Old or missing channel prices are reported, never guessed. Changing a price always needs you; StockChief never writes one.
88: Scores customer activity from comparable orders and product units actually shipped across two 30-day periods. Starter gets one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom get automatic owner notices when recent purchases decline.
89: Prepares scoped supplier messages about orders and follow-ups with fresh send authority. Live mailbox acceptance remains unverified.
90: Scores suppliers from actual warehouse deliveries, due-line fill, recorded price changes and invoice errors. Starter receives one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom can schedule the scorecard without training.
91: Compares verified supplier invoices and uploaded price lists with the approved PO or earlier trusted supplier price. Starter gets one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom surface higher comparable prices in owner review without training.
92: Compares current original supplier quotes for the same product, receiving site, quantity and currency. Shows goods rank, exact quoted delivery costs where recorded and links to the original. Growth reviews a draft. Pro and Custom can schedule comparisons without training.
93: Asks several suppliers for quotes when an item needs buying and you want competition: a new item, a purchase over your amount, or products or categories you name. Each RFQ states the item, quantity, needed-by date, delivery place and reply date. Replies in the RFQ’s format become quotations on their own; others wait for you to record them. Suppliers who do not reply get one reminder. Quotes are ranked side by side with links to the replies. It never accepts a price or places an order.
94: Drafts a negotiation email to a supplier from your records for the last 12 months: late deliveries against the agreed date, short deliveries, price increases on invoices and price lists, cheaper current quotes from other suppliers and how much you buy. Each fact links to its evidence and other suppliers are never named. You edit the draft and send it through your mailbox. It never orders, accepts or changes a price.
96: Reads known suppliers’ emails and attached files and keeps lead times, minimum orders, pack sizes, contact names and phone numbers current, with history and undo. Growth asks until taught; Pro and Custom update within your limits. A new order email address, prices, payment terms and anything unclear wait for you.
97: Tracks accepted rebate and volume-discount agreements against matched purchases, warns near the next tier, works out the rebate earned at period end, emails the claim within your limit and follows it to the supplier credit note. Growth gets a one-time estimate.
98: Reads original invoices from a connected mailbox, an owner upload or the private purchase link. Matches current purchase terms and actual receipts. Starter and Growth approve each bill. Pro and Custom can post clear matches within authorized rules without training.
99: Flags quantity, price and duplicate-invoice differences and keeps a disputed invoice out of the payment run.
100: Disputes supplier invoices that differ from the purchase order and receipts (wrong price, goods not received or billed twice, unagreed charges, wrong tax). Each message lists the evidence and the amount in question. The invoice stays out of the payment run. Reminders go out when the supplier does not answer. Replies, unclear evidence and disputes over your limit wait for you. A corrected invoice or a matching credit note settles it after your approval.
102: Sends payment reminders on your schedule: days before the due date, on it and days after, each step in its own words (yours, or a friendly, plain, gentle or firmer standard). Each uses the current balance, stops once the invoice is paid or the customer disputes it by email or you mark it, and stays within your balance limit. Growth drafts each due reminder for approval until one you approved is confirmed for that customer and mailbox, then sends alone; Pro and Custom send alone. A first B2B customer and Ask me first wait for you; pause, Watch only and the first 14 days only watch.
103: Matches imported statement credits to exact issued invoices, verifies the bank cash account, and records complete single or batch allocations together.
104: Prepares the upcoming supplier payment review from posted bills and documented discount deadlines. Growth prepares a draft for you to approve. Pro and Custom prepare it automatically. You approve the review and pay each supplier.
105: Tracks original supplier credit notes and unused balances, prepares the exact bill application, and verifies the owner-approved posting.
106: Shows recorded inventory value and identifies clearance candidates by SKU and location. It keeps stock needed for orders, transfers, rentals and replenishment out of the list and flags missing costs before decisions.
107: Prepares refunds and credits; a person approves each one. Returns are credited from the return; a lower or overcharged price credits the exact goods, discount share and tax from the posted invoice line, never shipping; money paid beyond a shipped order, or held by an order cancelled after payment, is refunded in full. Approval posts the credit note: unpaid amounts lower the invoice, paid ones go back through the original payments, via Stripe or Sola on their exact confirmation, or as an instruction you pay and record. StockChief never pays money itself.
108: Finds valid early-payment discounts in posted supplier bills and includes upcoming deadlines and possible savings in the payment run. Starter gets one suggestion. Growth, Pro and Custom get an automatic in-app alert.
109: Forecasts thirteen weeks of expected customer receipts and supplier payments by currency using posted balances, purchase goods and recorded charges. Pro and Custom can run the full forecast without training. Growth receives one suggestion. Missing dates or prices stay visible.
110: Compares monthly category budgets with posted supplier bill lines in the original currency. Growth, Pro and Custom flag category overspending in Needs You without training when monitoring is active. Starter offers one suggestion.
111: Turns a customer’s return email into an authorized return (RMA) with the order, items, quantities and reason. It checks the items actually left on that order and the owner’s return window and high-value limit. Unknown orders, items not on the order, late or high-value requests stop and ask in Needs you. Growth prepares each one until taught; Pro and Custom create them alone. Receiving the goods and refunds keep their own approvals.
112: For each authorized return whose goods went out by carrier, buys the cheapest return label through the connected shipping account, collected from the address the order went to once its address check is clear, and emails the customer the label and return steps. Growth prepares each one for a tap until taught; Pro and Custom act alone within the $ per label. Missing weight, an unconfirmed address, no rates or a first email to a new address stop and ask.
113: Decides restock, repair or scrap for each returned product from the condition staff recorded, by the owner’s rules: condition and, if chosen, product, return reason, goods value, time since the goods left and days before the batch expires. The most specific rule decides. Pro drafts until a completed manual example teaches a rule; Custom decides alone. Restock and repair moves happen on their own; scrap is a write-off and always waits for the owner.
114: After a person confirms the goods arrived, staff check each returned product on the phone. Products checked as good go back where they were sold from, through the return itself, with their batch, serials and cost. Growth prepares this for the owner to confirm; Pro and Custom do it on their own within the owner’s limit for good returns. Anything else stays held in quarantine for its own decision.
115: Prepares receipt-backed faulty-goods returns from verified supplier authorization. Pro learns from an individually completed return and posted credit. Custom can use explicit owner scope without training. A person confirms dispatch and approves each original credit note. StockChief tracks posted credits and what the supplier still owes.
116: Compares physically received returns with fulfilled goods by SKU and customer, keeping stocking units separate. Growth, Pro and Custom can flag two or more separate physical returns above the inventory’s same-unit peer rate in Needs You. Starter shows one suggestion.
117: Answers with a product’s recorded on-hand total and exact locations, including nested bins and independent weights. Open transfer quantities, supplier consignment, and customer custody have their own lines. Available on all plans without training.
118: Balances owned locations using their stock targets, usable costed goods, customer commitments, transfer and other holds, and dated incoming. Supports exact lots, serials, measured stock and recorded independent weights. An authorized request holds stock for separate approval and physical handling.
119: Requests and approves costed transfers within the owner’s chosen routes and exact stocking-unit limit. Checks protected targets, commitments, incoming supply, lots, serials and actual weights. Moves stocked kit components where the recipe and targets call for them. Staff confirm picking, dispatch and receipt.
120: Sets a product’s reorder point and target at the authorized location using actual local sales, recorded lead time, and exact stocking increments. Supports quantity, batch, serial and measured stock. Automatic changes stay within the owner’s saved target limit.
121: For each new or unassigned shipping order, picks the warehouse to ship from by the stock it really has free (after other orders, QC holds and protected stock), the distance to the customer and your warehouse priority and cost. Your rule decides when no single warehouse has it all: never split, or split when that ships sooner. The order and its reserved stock move there. It never changes an order being picked, asks when the address or facts are unclear, and every choice can be undone until picking starts.
122: Plans re-slots for each warehouse from 90 days of recorded picks, free stock, walking distance to packing and any checked bin fit. Each move goes to a closer empty bin in the same warehouse. An approved move reserves the stock in an ordinary transfer that staff pick, move and put away; unpicked moves can be undone. Pro approves each move or the whole list. Custom re-slots on a schedule within the owner’s move and unit limits. Batch, serial or expiry-tracked stock, reserved stock, stock being picked or counted, unchecked bins and over-limit moves wait for a person.
123: Compares recorded consignment counters with custody balances and shows separate dated ShipBob stock observations. Partner stock is not added to owned stock; live provider reconciliation remains open.
124: Checks dispatched transfers against physical receipts, loss and damage without training. Receiving staff see daily in-app follow-ups for assigned warehouses and can confirm they checked or record an actual arrival. Split receipts stay open for the exact remaining products, lots, serials and weights. A missing expected date is flagged separately. Physical receipt and write-offs retain their existing permissions.
125: Custom keeps one view of all its inventories or companies up to date on its own every 15 minutes: stock by product, matched by code or barcode; low stock and stockouts; and stock value, open purchase orders and sales for each currency, never added together. Products whose codes, barcodes or units disagree are shown side by side to check, not added up. Each person sees only the inventories and figures their access allows, can open the product in each inventory, and can download Excel or PDF. A pause or Ask me first waits for the owner. Lower plans see the plan lock.
126: Finds duplicate products (same barcode, supplier code, SKU or name), missing purchase costs and weights, and SKUs with spaces or characters channels reject. Fills a cost from the latest receipt or supplier price, and a weight from a supplier file or other sizes, only when every source agrees; otherwise it asks. A merge moves channel listings and supplier terms to the product kept and archives the copy with its history; stock is never moved. Starter suggests, Growth drafts a bulk fix list, Pro acts once taught, Custom acts within a daily limit. Every fix is audited and can be undone.
127: Creates products from a catalog or price list (CSV, spreadsheet or PDF) of a supplier you already have. New lines are created by the import with SKU, name, options, pack, cost and supplier link. Products you have are found by barcode, supplier code or SKU apart from capitals and spaces, linked and never duplicated; their cost and price stay. Missing facts, a name-only match and a changed supplier price or terms wait for you. Growth drafts the list for approval. Pro and Custom create exact lines on their own outside the first 14 days, Watch only, a pause and Ask me first. Audited and undoable.
129: Fills product specifications from approved supplier import columns, skipping unknown units, conflicting values and shared barcodes.
130: Creates mapped size and color variants from a reviewed supplier spreadsheet. Catalog creation does not post stock.
131: Gives new products a category and tags by fixed rules: one category in the product's own supplier file, or at least two similar products (same brand, supplier, material or name words) that all agree. Tags come from its own brand, material and file tags and tags all similar products carry. Growth, Pro and Custom set clear ones on their own within a daily limit you can change or stop; the rest wait as suggestions linking the similar products. Pause, the first 14 days, Watch only and Ask me first keep them waiting. Every change is logged and can be undone.
132: Retires a product when a checked supplier notice says so, when you mark it, or when its stock has not sold for the days in your dead-stock rule. It is never reordered again, the stock left is sold down (with a clearance plan whose prices you approve), and with none left and no open work it is archived and set to zero on your sales channels. Staff see the replacement on the product page, in order entry, on orders and pick lists, and in Ask. Open purchase orders and mismatched facts stop it; you decide any write-off. Logged and undoable.
133: Reads an import file and maps its columns from known headings, checks the values in every row fit each meaning, and reuses a mapping you approved for the same export, also when only the date in its name changes. Values that do not fit, or a column only the AI reader could place, stop the import until you answer. A column it does not know stops it mapping on its own and asks; approving keeps it as a product detail. Starter proposes the mapping for you to confirm. Growth, Pro and Custom map on their own, with an audit entry, outside the first 14 days, Watch only, a pause and Ask me first.
134: Converts saved supplier purchase units to exact stock units, including supported case and weight conversions, without posting stock.
135: Reads a supplier's price list in any format the price-list page accepts (spreadsheets, PDFs, documents and confirmed scans) and updates that supplier's future cost when the supplier, product and unit match exactly. Changes over 5%, or over the owner's lower limit for a supplier, wait for a person. Pro learns a supplier after one approved change and a saved limit; Custom needs no teaching. Unclear rows stop and ask, and an update can be undone until the cost changes again.
136: Saves quoted, product-matched facts from readable safety text and PDF specifications. It does not certify compliance or change prices, terms or physical stock.
137: Files supported bills of lading and customs PDF/text documents against their exact purchase order. Further formats and live provider polling remain open.
138: Classifies captured Gmail or Outlook messages as orders, invoices, questions, bulk mail or unknown senders. Live mailbox polling still needs verification.
142: Files supported original PDF/text documents on exact purchase, customer-order or product records. Uncertain target matches need separate confirmation; full live mailbox runs remain open.
144: Forecasts every product each day from its own confirmed orders and recorded sales, and tests each method on held-out days. With a year of history it follows yearly and weekday patterns. Each week's forecast is scored against what then sold. On Growth and up the forecasts drive the reorder list and the daily reorder point check. You can keep any product on plain sales history.
146: Forecasts each product added in the last 90 days from similar items with the same units and at least eight weeks of sales, chosen by you or by explicit rules: the same product, category or brand first, then a selling price within 25% and matching details. The similar items' own forecasts carry their seasons, and the new product's early sales count more each day. With no clear similar item it stops and asks you to choose one.
148: Checks every product each day: its last 14 days of confirmed orders and recorded sales against its own forecast from the history before them. A change of three standard deviations, at least 1.5 times faster on three or more sale days or half as slow, is a trend. One unusually large order is left out as a one-off. Trends go to Needs You, and while one lasts planning follows the recent pace until it eases or you dismiss it.
149: Models changes in sales demand, supplier lead time, or both. Shows the resulting demand and stock gap by warehouse, with links to the underlying items. Available in Ask and in the planning review.
150: Each day, after the forecasts, sets safety stock for every stocked product and location from your target for its A, B or C class: a percentage of reorders without running out, or how many times a year you can afford to run out. It uses how far sales stray from the forecast, how late deliveries came against their promised dates and the recorded lead time. The reorder point builds on it. Missing facts hold the change with the reason. Every change is logged and can be undone.
151: Every day, on every plan, works out when each item runs out: free stock after open orders and backorders, against the demand forecast day by day and purchase orders with a delivery date. It shows the next delivery, the gross margin lost each day without stock (selling price less cost) and in total before the delivery, and how many open customer orders would wait. Items that run out before their next delivery go to Needs You, ranked by that cost. Overdue or undated deliveries are listed but not counted.
153: Links supported Ask reviews to the exact filtered review and up to twelve visible underlying records. Other answer types still need evidence-link verification.
154: Builds a stock-by-location report from one sentence without AI credits. Supported custom reports can also be saved and charted. Live model qualification for open-ended requests still needs verification.
155: Emails saved reports to your account address on the schedule you choose. Each delivery shows its status, and the worker checks your current report and recipient before sending. The workflow has been tested on every plan with simulated email delivery. Live mailbox delivery is still unverified.
156: Delivers the previous business day's purchases, customer orders, shipments, stock activity, and completed work in Needs you. Lists the approvals waiting and overdue records when the briefing ran.
157: Explains why sales, gross profit, cost of goods or stock value changed between two months, for the business or one item, channel, customer or warehouse, on the page and in Ask. It splits the change into volume, mix, selling price, cost per unit, discounts, returns and other postings, or the stock roll-forward, adding up exactly, each linked to its records. Cost changes link to receipts, landed costs and supplier price increases; write-offs, channel fees and likely stockouts are shown too. After each month ends it flags changes of 20% or more in Needs you.
158: Makes the month-end stock value and cost of goods report after each month ends: for each location, opening value, received, cost of goods sold, counts and adjustments, written off, transfers and closing value, from the stock records, leaving out later postings. Totals are checked against Inventory in your books; postings only in the books are listed and any difference is flagged in Needs you until a later check clears it. Download it as Excel or PDF. Closing the month in your books stays with you.
159: Custom builds a board or investor pack as a PDF with charts: six months of sales, gross profit and margin, cash tied up in stock, days of supply and stock turns, the best items, and problems from the records (write-offs, count differences, a books difference, overdue invoices, items out of stock), with a short commentary written only from those numbers. Each currency has its own pages. Download it any time, keep a copy, or choose a day each month and StockChief builds the pack for the month that just ended and tells you in Needs you.
160: Download saved answers, including short text replies, on a phone or computer. Excel and CSV retain readable text when a character is unavailable in the PDF font.
161: Makes the ROI report for each month that ends, on every plan. Hours saved count each finished agent task times your own timed minutes, or StockChief's standard minutes marked as estimates. Money caught lists each amount with its record: supplier credits from claims, disputes and returns, applied credit notes, rebates, claim refunds, corrected invoices, duplicate invoices stopped, freight saved and proven stock-outs avoided. Both are compared with your plan price, each currency apart. The worker tells you in Needs you, and by email when alerts are on. Excel and PDF downloads.
162: Shows stock turns, gross margin return on inventory (GMROI) and days of supply for each item at each location, over up to the last 90 days, from the stock value records, posted sales and cost of goods, and stock on hand. Bins count with their warehouse. When goods carry no cost or the records disagree, the money ratios are withheld. Growth, Pro and Custom check every item each day on their own and flag in Needs you up to five that earn back less than they cost to hold. Starter gets one suggestion.
163: Shows how close StockChief's saved weekly forecasts came to what sold (MAPE and bias, per product and overall; weeks with no sales and stock-out weeks counted apart), and fill rate and on-time-in-full for customers, from orders against shipments, and for suppliers, from purchase orders against receipts. Orders without a promised date are left out and counted. Growth, Pro and Custom keep the month so far and the last month current on their own each day and keep each month's figures. Download it as Excel or PDF, or read it in Ask.
164: Builds a shareable PDF for one supplier and any completed calendar quarter. Includes placed orders, agreed costs and quantities received by quarter close. Download it to send to that supplier.
165: Downloads an accountant workbook with the selected fiscal year's posted closing stock and in-transit values, approved physical-count records, and completed warehouse worksheets, including annual stocktake worksheets. Pending counts stay out of the workbook.
166: Alerts you on its own, on every plan, when a product falls to its reorder point, or to your own alert level when it has none, and when it runs out. StockChief checks through the day, turns a low-stock alert into a stock-out and clears it when stock recovers. Alerts show on the alert page and in Needs you. Choose a connected mailbox and new alerts are emailed to you. Emails wait during the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first; with Ask me first you can send them yourself.
167: Watches what you describe in plain words, on its own on every plan: any item, or a brand, category, supplier, location or tag, for stock under, over or out, a selling price change, sales above or below a number over a day, week or month, or a batch expiring within some days. It reads the rule without guessing, shows how it read it and asks back when a name or number is unclear. It checks rules through the day and alerts in the app, in Needs you and by email, like stock alerts. Rules count against your plan's rule allowance; Starter gets 5.
168: Alerts you on its own, on every plan, to purchase orders past their expected date with goods still to come, customer orders not shipped by the date promised, shipped parcels past their delivery date, and customer invoices and supplier bills unpaid past their due date. Each alert carries its date, follows changes, is reminded daily and clears when goods arrive, the order ships or is delivered, or the invoice is paid. Alerts show on the page and in Needs you, and are emailed to you from the mailbox you choose. Emails wait during the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first.
169: Alerts you on its own, on every plan, when a channel shows more of a product than you can sell (after orders, protected stock, holds and your channel buffer) and when a channel's sync is paused, needs a new sign-in, failed, went quiet or stopped sending orders, or a stock update failed. It checks through the day and clears each alert once fixed. Alerts show on their page and in Needs you, and are emailed from the mailbox you choose; emails wait during the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first, where you can send them yourself.
170: Alerts you on its own, on Growth, Pro and Custom, when a cost rises by your percentage or more: the saved purchase cost, the cost of goods received with their freight and duty, or a supplier's new price waiting for review. It also alerts when gross margin, before fees and shipping, falls under your percentage for an item, a category or a sales channel. Costs in different currencies are never compared. Alerts clear when no longer true, show in Needs you and are emailed from your mailbox; emails wait in the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first. Starter is excluded.
171: Alerts you on its own, on Pro and Custom, to activity that looks unusual in the last seven days: a stock correction or selling price change over your limit or three times what is usual for that product, one person making your number of changes or deletions in a day or three times their usual, and anything changed in the hours you watch. Logins are not recorded, so they are not checked. Nothing is blocked. Alerts are audited, show in Needs you and are emailed from your mailbox; emails wait in the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first.
172: On Pro and Custom, once you choose how many hours to wait, passes any alert or approval in your Needs you that nobody answers to the next person on its own: the team member with the right permission and enough approval limit, least senior first, then back to you. Each person gets the same wait, sees it in Needs you and gets an email from your mailbox; "I'm on it" or dealing with it stops it. Purchase signatures keep their own window. Passing on waits in the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first, where you can pass an item on yourself. Every step is audited.
173: Sends alerts by text and push as well as email, on every plan; you choose for each kind of alert, including items passed on and approvals. Each person confirms their mobile number with a texted code and turns push on in each browser. Alerts go to you; passed-on items and approvals go to whoever has them. Texts and push wait in the first 14 days, pause, Watch only and Ask me first, where you can send them yourself; each is checked again before it goes out and never sent twice. Live sending needs the server's Twilio account and push keys.
174: Needs you is one list of every decision: purchase orders, transfers, returns and prepared changes waiting for approval join the rest, and below Pro they all go to the owner. Similar approvals for the same person (same kind and supplier, route or location, each within that person's limits) are approved or declined in one tap; each still goes through its own service and checks, and any that fail stay with the reason. Two-person approvals and Ask conversations are decided one by one. No groups in the first 14 days or Watch only.
175: Sends each approval waiting in someone's Needs you to them once, by email, text or push as you choose, on every plan, with its own link. Opening it approves nothing; the person signs in and sees it as it is now. Purchase orders, transfers, second purchase signatures and suggested QC holds approve with one tap, checked again against the person's permission, limit and any change since they looked; each is audited and recorded once. Other approvals open their own page. Sending waits in the first 14 days, Watch only and Ask me first.
176: Sends every waiting approval (purchases, stock adjustments and write-offs, refunds and credits, landed costs, supplier prices, transfers, returns) to one person: the owner's rule first ("refunds over $500 go to Sarah"), else the team member with its permission, the whole inventory and the lowest limit that covers it, else the owner. Limits are checked again on approval. The first 14 days, Watch only, pause and Ask me first keep everything with the owner. Each reviewer is audited.
177: Gives staff tasks of every main kind: pick this order or wave, put away this receipt, inspect this delivery held for QC, move stock to the right bin, and count this shelf. Each task goes to a team member who can do that work and reach its warehouse, shows on their phone and in Needs you, and is checked off only when the work’s own record shows it done: the wave scanned, the put-away confirmed, the inspection recorded, the move scanned, the count saved. Tasks past their due time are flagged to the owner and the person. The owner can assign, decline or withdraw any task.
178: Writes step-by-step procedures for receiving, picking, dispatch, counting and customer returns from how your team really works: the scans, QC checks, put-aways, phone counts and return decisions recorded around each completed example. A step done in most examples becomes a step, in the order staff did it; rarer ones become notes. Nothing is invented: with no recorded examples, nothing is written. You can edit the staff text, and go back to an earlier staff version.
179: Answers supported inventory and warehouse how-to questions from the in-app guide, filtered by current plan, role and warehouse access.
180: Delivers a daily team summary in Needs you. Shows stock activity by staff member, verified warehouse tasks by who finished them, and overdue assignments by who is responsible, with links to review the work.
181: Traces supported stock and purchase-cost changes through the authenticated audit trail and CSV. Complete reasoning and undo across all action types remain open.
184: Exports a reviewed journal through the QuickBooks adapter and verifies its recorded result. Live QuickBooks, Xero and invoice/bill synchronization remain unqualified.
185: Supports Orderful test-stream order, acknowledgment, ship-notice and invoice flows. Retailer certification and authenticated sandbox acceptance remain open; Pro needs the EDI add-on.
186: Supports the ShipBob test adapter for order submission, duplicate-response recovery, split tracking and stock reads. Live sandbox qualification and other 3PLs remain open.
187: Prepares sender-specific unsent replies from supported captured Gmail or Outlook messages. Live model and mailbox qualification remain open.
189: Lets an authorized Custom API client start registered reviews, including a supplier lead-time scenario or a past supplier-report quarter, and receive signed completion webhooks. Review jobs only read business records.
190: Moves your data in from your old system’s CSV and Excel exports: products, stock by location with value, suppliers, customers, open purchase and sales orders (sales orders unconfirmed), unpaid invoices and bills, and opening books. An unknown table, unreadable value or missing total stops and asks. Records are checked against the export’s totals and every saved balance against the records; a difference stops and asks. Growth drafts the plan; you approve and open the inventory. Pro and Custom do both on their own when all matches, outside the first 14 days, Watch only, a pause and Ask me first.
191: Warns before batches expire, using the warning days you set for every product, a category or one product (30 days if you set none), in the app, in Needs you and by email from your connected mailbox. Each warning shows where to sell first: orders due before it expires, other locations with orders, the channels it is listed on, and a clearance plan for what will be left. Picks take the soonest expiry first. Emails wait during shadow mode, pause, Watch only and Ask me first.
192: Reserves exact FIFO receipt layers or FEFO lots and serials at existing allocated locations, including variants, kits and measured goods. Protects competing commitments; missing age, expiry, cost and independent weight need evidence. Physical picking, stock and value changes remain separate.
193: Finds the customers, quantities and original sales or custody records for an exact lot. Covers warehouse and supplier-direct orders, kit components, rental and outgoing consignment, including goods later returned.
194: Blocks recalled or expired batches on every way out: picks and shipments, transfers to another location, the quantity offered on sales channels, kit components, rentals and consignment. Only a write-off or a return to the supplier takes them out. A person places a recall; releasing one always needs a person and a reason, and both are audited. Open transfers and reservations that still name a blocked batch show in Needs you. Blocks hold in every mode, including pause and shadow mode.
195: Shows recorded receipts, both legs of transfers, issues, supplier-direct dispatches and returns for an exact serial, ordered by time and linked to the original product or order.
196: Tracks required lot certificates and flags missing or expired evidence when the recorded documents change.
197: Prepares a compliance report for any period from your records: where each batch came from and went, recall decisions and who received recalled batches, expiry write-offs, stock adjustments with who and why, stocktake sign-offs and quality checks. Each report is frozen and downloads as Excel or PDF. Growth drafts each report for you to finalize. Pro and Custom produce them weekly or monthly on their own. A stock removal with no recorded reason, shadow mode, pause or Ask me first leaves the report as a draft for you.
198: For a new account's first 14 days StockChief only watches. Reorders, transfers, counts, count lists, credit and delivery holds, payment reminders and tracking emails record what they would have done, with amounts. A report shows the orders it would have placed, the stockouts it would have prevented (from your stock records) and the money it would have caught. When the 14 days end, Needs you asks you to switch on automatic work per area or for everything, or keep watching. Switched-on areas get your plan's highest mode; the rest keep watching, and spending still needs your limits.
199: Every purchase order, transfer, count posting and tracking email shows how sure StockChief is: high, medium or low, with reasons from the facts that action checks: prices and stock, missing facts, earlier orders, counts and delivered emails. When a required fact is missing or does not match it is low and always asks. You choose whether it may act on its own when fairly sure or only when very sure; below that it asks instead. The level shows on the review pages, in Needs you and in Ask.
200: Gives a data health score from 0 to 100 on day one, worked out by the worker after each import, once a day and when you ask. Every active product is checked for a usable SKU, a unique barcode, a purchase cost, a weight, not being a duplicate, a supplier, a reorder point, stock not below zero and a count in the last year, with the result for each check. A fix list puts the most urgent first and links to where each fix is made, mostly the bulk fixes for product data. The score shows on its own in Needs you and on its page on every plan, also while StockChief only watches.
201: Pauses routine work when recorded automatic purchasing, postage or action volume exceeds its recent range. Counts verified standing-rule actions, excludes manually approved work and retries, and shows the owner why it paused before they resume.
202: Sends eligible approvals to your deputy’s Needs you list on the dates you choose. StockChief checks their current permissions and amount limits for purchases, transfers, returns, and other approvals in the approval desk. Owner-only decisions stay with the owner.
203: Restricts supported cost columns, filters, reports, source imports and financial reads by role. A full document, mail and export disclosure audit remains open.
204: Shows supported completed agent work by business day and can undo an unchanged draft or the latest eligible purchase-cost update. Other effects require their recorded correction workflow.
205: Two different people, each allowed to approve it, must approve anything over the owner's amount: purchase orders, refunds and credits, stock adjustments and write-offs, and landed-cost postings from any page or routine. Anything in another currency, or whose amount is unknown, also needs two. Each approval is bound to the exact amount, so a change needs fresh approvals, and the same person twice counts once. The second approval goes to the next eligible person's Needs you; where only the owner may post, the owner posts last.
206: Finds repeat approved purchase regroupings each month and estimates future review time from owner timing samples. Teaching the matching rule clears the suggestion.
207: Saves supported plain-language reorder instructions within the account's shared rule allowance. Other plain-language rule types still need qualification.
208: Learns bounded quotation, production-draft and supplier-price scopes from completed approvals and preserves the owner's limits. Further routine types need separate qualification.
209: Suggests a recurring blind count after repeated non-opening quantity corrections for the same product and warehouse. Other correction patterns remain open.
210: Tests a draft purchase-consolidation rule against recorded completed work before enabling it. Historical simulations for other rule types remain open.
211: Uses confirmed orders and completed receipts to learn when each customer usually orders and how quickly each supplier delivers. Shows estimated next order dates and supplier reliability against promised delivery dates.
213: Runs your saved sequence of eligible operational reviews on demand or on a daily or weekly schedule. It remembers filters on supported steps and checks the current plan and owner permissions each time. Growth includes up to ten playbooks.
214: Remembers each Custom manager's report period, preferred download format and approval-inbox sort within the inventory. Applies preferences to the reports dashboard, standard reports, saved report downloads and Needs you. Explicit choices take precedence.
